results.title: Section 232 Auto & Auto Parts Tariffs: What Importers Need to Know in 2026 - Sobel Network Shipping Co., Inc.
results.content:
## Commercial Vehicles Are Included

Contrary to some assumptions, commercial vehicles are not excluded from Section 232 duties.

Covered vehicles include:

 Sedans
 SUVs and crossover vehicles
 Minivans
 Cargo vans
 Light trucks

If classified under the relevant HTS provisions, these vehicles remain subject to Section 232 duties regardless of commercial use.

## Special Cases: Government Employees & Military Personnel [...] Only auto parts for passenger vehicles and light trucks that are subject to Section 232 duties qualify for exemption from reciprocal tariffs under HTS heading 9903.01.33.

This means:

 Not all auto parts are exempt
 Zero-rate Chapter 99 classifications alone do not guarantee exemption
 Aluminum derivative classifications with zero aluminum content do not automatically qualify

Eligibility depends on both the product category and its Section 232 status, not just tariff rate. [...] Passenger vehicles
 Light trucks
 Certain auto parts classified under specific HTS subheadings

Used vehicles are also covered, with one key exception: vehicles manufactured 25 years or more prior to the year of entry are excluded.

## Reciprocal Tariffs vs. Section 232: A Key Distinction

One of the most important clarifications for 2025 is how reciprocal tariffs interact with Section 232 duties.

results.title: Section 232 Automotive Tariffs: Issues for Congress
results.content:
The following U.S. tariffs do not apply to goods subject to Section 232 automotive tariffs:

   Other Section 232 tariffs (e.g., steel, aluminum, copper); and
   Temporary global tariffs under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974.

Unless otherwise agreed, Section 232 automotive tariffs are in addition to

   MFN tariffs;
   Trade remedies; and 
   Tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. [...] with 25% tariffs on non-USMCA-compliant vehicles imported from the United States and the non-Canadian, non-Mexican content of U.S. vehicles traded under USMCA. Other auto groups have called for further tariff reductions. [...] In 2025, President Donald Trump imposed 25% tariffs on U.S. imports of automobiles and certain automobile parts under Section 232. Section 232 authorizes the President to take action (e.g., tariffs, quotas, or negotiations) if the Secretary of Commerce determines that imports of a good "threaten to impair" U.S. national security. President Trump imposed auto tariffs based on the findings of a 2019 investigation, which concluded that U.S. auto imports were a threat to U.S. national security.
